convoLines.text: "Can I trust you? I mean really."
"That's the right answer. The wrong one would've been 'yes' too fast. That's the priority."
"I'll tell you what I tell everyone: watch what I do when nobody's watching. That's the whole of me. The rest is just talking."
"Still on whether they can trust you."
"I can't. Not today. Ask me when the work's done."
"Look, forget it. You wanted something?"
"Have you heard what they're calling The Living Wire? I'm pushing 'Big Ugly'. Everyone's got a name for it and nobody agrees."
"I see." They take a moment to think about your answer.
You show them Black Walnut — where it grows, how to tell it apart. "Huh." They turn it over in their mind. "I'll remember that one."
"I have opinions about the name. I am saving them for when they count."
"We'll land on something. We always do — usually the loudest person's idea."
"Well. My social battery is officially dead."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"This was good." They mean it.
"Can I tell you something? Before the scattering, I ran when I should have stayed. I think about it every day."
"Thank you for hearing it. I needed someone to know — and I needed it to stop with you."
"What do you miss most? From before."
"Take your time."
"So what's your plan here? Just... get through it?"
"Permit me: Honest. I can work with honest."
"Still on that question. That is all."
"Anyway — that's my problem, not yours. What did you want?"
"Huh. Let me think about that." "Have you heard what they're calling The Living Wire? Ruby is pushing 'Big Ugly'. Everyone's got a name for it and nobody agrees."
"All right. Thank you for telling me."
"A name. Okay." You say it out loud, trying the shape of it:
🤝 "The Company." It hangs in the air a moment — then Ashanti grins. It's real now. It has a name, which means it can be lost.
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
"Right. Go on, then."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"When's the last time you really laughed?"
"Stealing joy. I like that. We should steal more of it."
"Three days ago. Someone dropped a whole basket of tubers and we just stood there laughing. It wasn't even funny. It was the standing there."
"Still on the last time you laughed. Just my read."
"Out there? I'd rather not die today, thanks."
"Probably — Forget it — go on, I'm listening."
"The whole fire was arguing about The Living Wire last night — what to even CALL it. 'The Ugly Beast' got shouted down. What's your vote?"
"Let me sit with all that. We'll pick it up later."
They fill the quiet. "Anyway — where was I?"
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"See you around."
"What got you through the first week? The very first days."
"Shock's underrated. It's the body's way of buying you time, as it were."
"Honestly? I don't think anything got me through. I just didn't stop. Some mornings that's the whole story — you keep not-stopping until not-stopping feels like a plan."
"Still on what got you through the first week."
"Never mind. You had something to say?"
The easy manner evaporates. What's left is watching you back.
"I don't actually want to belong somewhere. I want to keep the peace. It's safer if people don't know. Please don't tell the others."
"I don't know you well enough for that. Ask me again when we've survived something together."
"That again?" Esteban sighs. "I confessed that already. I'm not confessing it twice for dramatic effect."
Esteban looks at you, level. "I told you the truth. You can keep poking it, but it's told."
"You're a good listener, you know that?" A tired smile.
"Right. Go on, then."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"Same time tomorrow, maybe."
"About that question — Are you angry? At whoever did this. At the sky. At anything."
"Good. Anger's fuel. Just — point it somewhere useful. Good talking."
The ease drains out of it, a little.
"Still on whether you're angry. Be kind to yourself, okay?"
"That can wait — it isn't going anywhere. What's on your mind?"
"Huh. I answered that once — back when the answer was simpler." "The whole fire was arguing about Flashbulb Moth last night — what to even CALL it. 'Loud-Eyes' got shouted down. What's your vote?"
"Take your time."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
"The fire'll settle it. It settles everything, eventually."
🤝 Ashanti is 👁️ Scout now. Sees trouble first. Warns the party on the road.
"My vote? I'm keeping it to myself until the shouting stops."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"This was good." They mean it.
"Hey — I found some Black Walnut today. You were right, it was right where you said. No time to waste."
They nod slowly, not quite done, not quite continuing.
"Still on that plant lesson. Extremely normal, all of it."
They take it in and give nothing back. Not yet.
"Another time. The village needs me here."
You show them Elderberry — where it grows, how to tell it apart. Their eyes widen. "I never knew that."
"Go ahead — you've got my attention. Allegedly."
"You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "Have you heard what they're calling Flashbulb Moth? I'm pushing 'Loud-Eyes'. Everyone's got a name for it and nobody agrees."
They nod. "Okay."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Sure. I'll be around."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"You said one day at a time. How's that holding — still day by day, or are you thinking further out yet?"
"Take your time."
They nod slowly, not quite done, not quite continuing.
"Still on that personal stuff."
"Yeah? What's up?"
"Last time things were different. They always are." "The whole fire was arguing about The Static Kite last night — what to even CALL it. 'Big-Eyes' got shouted down. What's your vote?"
They nod, giving you room to think.
"That's... pretty much all of it, honestly."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Rest when you can. We'll talk again soon."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."

"We never did finish talking about what's been happening — that was 8 days back. Still on your mind? 'Have you heard what they're calling Flashbulb Moth? I'm pushing 'Loud-Eyes'. Everyone's got a name for it and…'"
Ruby has an edge today — something curdled.
"I wish there was more to tell. That's it."
"Right — go on, I'm listening."
"You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "Have you heard what they're calling The Static Kite? I'm pushing 'Big-Eyes'. Everyone's got a name for it and nobody agrees."
"All right. Thank you for telling me."
"We started on what's been happening, then got onto that question. But what do I know."
"Okay. Yeah. I trust you."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"And... scene. Good talk."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"This was good." They mean it.
"You said shock got you through the first week. Just kept moving. What's carrying you now?"
"Take your time."
They hear you out, but something in them stays guarded.
"So." They look at the fire for a moment.
"Still on that personal stuff."
"Okay. Yeah. I trust you."
You show them Black Walnut — where it grows, how to tell it apart. Their eyes widen. "I never knew that."
"Alright, I'm listening. What's next?"
"You want to know about that? Okay." "Have you heard what they're calling The Static Kite? Ruby is pushing 'Big-Eyes'. Everyone's got a name for it and nobody agrees."
They nod. "Okay."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
Ashanti nods, stepping back. "Scout is yours now." (Roles are promises. There's only one of each.)
"I'm staying out of the naming fight. For now. Someone always gets precious about their pick."
"Alright — carefully, now. Both of us."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."

lines: d6: Nobody's talking much. The fire feels smaller tonight.
d6: 🕯️ Heinrich Stepanov is dead — the expedition. The village stops. Somebody screams. Somebody else starts digging.
d6: What Heinrich kept close goes into the ground with them — keepsakes are buried, never taken from the body.
d6: "Heinrich's gone." Ruby looks at you for a long moment. "You're not Heinrich." No heat in it. Just fact. You'll have to earn this face.
d6: Grace picks up the journal. Their hands shake. Then they open it, and keep writing.

d6: 📖 LEARNED: Diplomatic Incident (Level 1). Trust builds 2x faster. You're TOO good though — once per week you can start a diplomatic incident: villagers argue, you pick the winner (+trust with them, -trust with the loser).
d6: 📖 LEARNED: Reading People (Level 1). Microexpressions leak truth. Watch the eyes, not the mouth. People tell you who they are.
d6: ⚡ TECHNIQUE UNLOCKED: Deep Read! You don't just read trust — you read intent. Know what they'll do next. (Your knowledge of Reading People amplifies your open_book.)
d6: 📖 LEARNED: Calming Panic (Level 1). Ground them: 5 things you see, 4 you hear, 3 you touch. Breathe with them. Slow is fast.
d6: 📖 LEARNED: Mediation (Level 1). Let each side talk without interruption. Repeat back what you heard. People de-escalate when heard.
d6: 📖 LEARNED: Keeping Morale (Level 1). People need small wins. Celebrate the little things. Despair is the real killer.
d6: 🌟 "MANTLE TRANSFER DETECTED. ...Oh! New face! Same job! Whole new set of tricks. We hardly noticed. (That is a lie. We noticed. The audience CRIED.)"
d6: 📖 The Codex turns a page: Heinrich Stepanov, 6 days. The mantle passes to Grace Obi.
d6: 🪞 You wake up somebody else. Grace Obi, 43 — an ESL teacher. Her hands know different work now: Beast-calm.
d6: At the grave, Ruby, Ashanti speak for Grace — "Heinrich trusted them. We saw it. Give them the fire's hearing." The village listens.
d6: The fire knew Grace before the Codex did — her name already carried weight here.

lastSay: d31: 🎁 You find a small bundle tucked where you'll find it. No one saw it left there.
d31: "They're sending Vex after you tomorrow. He's bored. Be somewhere else."
d31: (400 kcal of dried meat and clean water. Nothing traceable.)
d31: Snow by morning. (3°C — Cold) The ground goes iron — forage thin, walking dear.
d31: Dawn. You wake rested. (+0 health, energy restored. By the fire. Good enough.)
